title: Classic Maki Sushi: Tuna, Salmon and Cucumber Hosomaki Rolls
summary: Thin nori rolls of seasoned sushi rice with a single strip of tuna, salmon or cucumber, cut into neat pieces and served with soy sauce, wasabi and pickled ginger.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
cucumber, seeds removed, cut into 1 cm batons

steps.title: Rinse and drain
steps.text: Wash the rice in several changes of cold water until it runs almost clear and drain it for 15 min. This clears away excess starch so the cooked rice is sticky enough to hold but not pasty.

steps.title: Steam the rice
steps.text: Boil the rice with 480 ml water in a heavy covered pan, then cook on the lowest heat for 12 min. Leave it covered off the heat for 10 min more so the grains finish softening in their own steam.

steps.title: Dress the rice
steps.text: Dissolve the sugar and salt in the vinegar over a low heat. Spread the hot rice in the wide bowl, sprinkle the seasoning over and fold it in with slicing strokes while fanning; this cools it quickly and makes it shine. Cover with a damp cloth once it reaches body temperature.

steps.title: Crisp the nori
steps.text: Pass each sheet a few times over a gas flame or under a hot grill (broiler) for a few seconds, until it smells toasty and turns brittle. Halve the sheets along the lines to make 8 strips.

steps.title: Fill and roll
steps.text: On the film-wrapped mat, lay a half sheet shiny side down and, with damp fingers, spread about 100 g rice thinly over it, leaving 1 cm uncovered at the top and bottom. Put one filling along the near third, lift the mat to tuck the edge over it and roll forward firmly, sealing the bare edge with a little water; make 3 tuna, 3 salmon and 2 cucumber rolls.

steps.title: Cut and serve
steps.text: Wipe the knife with a damp cloth, cut each roll in half and each half into three, wiping the blade between cuts so the rice does not drag. Serve at once with soy sauce, wasabi and pickled ginger.

tips: RAW NOTE: the fish is eaten raw. Buy sushi- or sashimi-grade fish from a fishmonger you trust that has been frozen first (-20 °C for 7 days or -35 °C for 15 hours), keep it in the fridge until the last minute and eat it the same day. Pregnant people, young children, older adults and anyone with weakened immunity should skip it.
Do not overfill; a single 1 cm strip of filling is enough for a half sheet, or the roll will split.
Spread the rice loosely with fingertips rather than pressing it, so the rolls stay light.
Use cucumber or avocado alone for a vegetarian roll.
storage: Sushi rolls are best eaten within an hour of rolling; discard leftovers containing raw fish. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
